page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 1 dedicated vCPU and 4 GB of RAM. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, this instance provides 1 physical core with 1 thread per core. The CPU architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, but lacks AVX-512 support. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data highlights a strong single-core performance profile, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the top 25% at 2647.38. However, due to its single-vCPU limitation, multi-core benchmarks are constrained, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Single-threaded tasks perform moderately, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the middle 50%. Text processing and LLM text generation for a small 135M model also achieve average tier results, while database operations, image processing, and static web serving throughput register in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-1 offers a dedicated CPU allocation at a low resource density, making it a viable option for lightweight workloads that require predictable single-core performance without the CPU-sharing overhead of burstable instances. It is best suited for basic web serving, lightweight background workers, single-threaded scripting tasks, and small-scale development or testing environments that do not require high memory capacity or multi-threaded processing power.
